questions.question: Why do users add to wishlist?
questions.answer: Deferred intent — a price/occasion holding pen, not impulse.

questions.question: What prevents purchase?
questions.answer: Price gap vs other platforms; size unavailable in their size.

questions.question: What uncertainties remain?
questions.answer: Whether the price is genuinely good, and whether their size stays in stock.

questions.question: What causes postponement?
questions.answer: Waiting for a sale; size out of stock; comparing elsewhere.

questions.question: How do users compare shortlisted products?
What info sought outside Myntra?
questions.answer: Prices on other apps; reviews/YouTube for fit and quality.

questions.question: Role of fit/size/styling/price/reviews/occasion/social validation?
questions.answer: Price, size and comparison strongly present; styling and social validation NOT strongly surfaced in public text.

questions.question: Wishlist as genuine intent vs bookmark?
questions.answer: Both — large unpruned lists used as bookmarks, alongside sale-triggered buying.

questions.question: How do behaviours differ across segments?
questions.answer: Not resolvable from public text alone — carried to interviews.

questions.question: What unmet needs recur?
questions.answer: Users repeatedly leave Myntra to verify price/value elsewhere before buying.

verbatims.text: Saved it for later, waited for a sale — but by the time the price dropped the size was gone, so I bought the same thing cheaper elsewhere.
Sizes are not available for many of my liked products.
Prices are slightly higher than other platforms — I cross-check before buying.
The offer showed on the app, but two days later at booking it was auto-cancelled.
1,000-item wishlist cap stopped me from saving more.
Wishlisted item shows a higher price than its sibling colours.
I’ll wait for the December End of Reason Sale before buying what’s saved.
Bought it straight from the wishlist because it was sale time.

steps.title: Scrape sources
steps.body: Play/App Store v1+v2 merged, plus YouTube and Reddit, into one schema.

steps.title: Relevance pass
steps.body: LLM tags each item: is this real save-then-decide behaviour? Not sentiment.

steps.title: Strict re-read
steps.body: Separate genuine deferral from generic mentions. Counts corrected down.

steps.title: Manual audit
steps.body: Hand-tag a sample, compare to the model, report the agreement rate.

engine.note: The live pipeline runs from the project repo (scrapers + classification scripts). This page is the findings surface — it presents the output of that run so it can be read and interrogated without re-running collection. Classification is fact-constrained: the model tags and quotes, it doesn't invent items.
